scenarios.title: A W3D nested in a BIG archive opens as a subject
scenarios.evidence: the archive itself opens, but the extension exposes no command or URI shape that names an entry inside it — «data/editor/molds/bowl.w3d» is unreachable from outside the page, and inside the page the archive stage reads an entry’s bytes into a hex pane rather than opening it as a subject. The host route exists and Electron uses it; this product does not wire it, so nested opening is absent here (wiring missing, blocks 13–14)

diagnosticsChannel.note: the handler calls bridge.emit only, so a subject diagnostic reaches the extension host’s output channel and is never drawn on the page’s status bar — invisible to the user, and unreadable to any observer, because an OutputChannel has no read API

nestedSubjectRoute.note: the VS Code archive stage reads an entry’s bytes into a hex pane; it never opens the entry as a subject, so no descriptor, no stages and no nested diagnostics exist for it

absolutePathCheck.scope: the diagnostic lines themselves, not the whole page — the breadcrumb legitimately shows the opened file’s location, while a diagnostic is what travels into logs
